key_insight: A 3D physics-informed neural network couples patient-specific pulmonary blood flow with Windkessel outlet dynamics by separating basal pressure from local pressure variations.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports meshless hemodynamic modeling and outlet-parameter estimation toward patient-specific cardiovascular digital twins.
method: Embed flow equations and Windkessel RCR outlet dynamics in PINN training.
Decompose pressure and impose a Windkessel initial condition, pressure gauge, and global mass balance.
Use periodic Fourier time embedding for pulsatile flow.
evidence_signal: Tests on 2D channels and a patient-specific right pulmonary artery showed flow-field errors on the order of data resolution; inverse tests recovered three Windkessel parameters from synthetic data with about 0.3% error.
watch_item: Local pressure biases persist, and robustness to noisy clinical data remains untested.
paper_title: A 3D PINN-Based Framework for Patient-Specific Pulmonary Hemodynamics Using Windkessel Models
